topic_tag: circle defined as a set of points by a distance ratio
subskill: derive a circle's equation from PA = 2PB, then its radius
prompt: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, point A is at (−3, 6) and point B is at (1, −2). The set of all points P for which the distance from P to A is twice the distance from P to B is a circle. To the nearest hundredth of a coordinate unit, what is the radius of this circle?
explanation: Squaring PA = 2PB gives (x + 3)² + (y − 6)² = 4[(x − 1)² + (y + 2)²]. Expanding, x² + y² + 6x − 12y + 45 = 4x² + 4y² − 8x + 16y + 20, so 3x² + 3y² − 14x + 28y − 25 = 0. Dividing by 3: x² + y² − (14/3)x + (28/3)y − 25/3 = 0. Completing the square, the center is (7/3, −14/3) and r² = 49/9 + 196/9 + 25/3 = 320/9, so r = √320/3 ≈ 5.96. The option "6.37" multiplies the x², y² and x, y terms on the right by 4 but leaves the constant 5 unmultiplied. The option "4.71" multiplies only the x² and y² terms on the right by 4. The option "7.23" divides the x², y², x and y terms by 3 but not the constant −25.

prompt: The top of a lighthouse is 46.8 meters above sea level, and F is the point at sea level directly below the top. From the top of the lighthouse, the angle of depression to boat P is 10° and the angle of depression to boat Q is 16°. Boats P and Q are 261 meters apart. To the nearest hundredth of a degree, what is the measure of ∠PFQ ?
explanation: The horizontal distances are FP = 46.8/tan 10° ≈ 265.42 m and FQ = 46.8/tan 16° ≈ 163.21 m. topic_tag: running fix from two bearings (law of sines)
subskill: bearings to triangle angles; law of sines
prompt: A ship sails due east at a constant speed of 14 kilometers per hour. At 9:00 a.m., a lighthouse is on a bearing of 047° from the ship (that is, 47° clockwise from due north). At 10:25 a.m., the lighthouse is on a bearing of 352° from the ship. To the nearest hundredth of a kilometer, how far is the ship from the lighthouse at 10:25 a.m.?
explanation: From 9:00 to 10:25 is 1 hour 25 minutes = 85/60 hour, so the ship travels 14(85/60) ≈ 19.833 km from S1 to S2. At S1 the course (bearing 090°) and the line to the lighthouse L (bearing 047°) form an angle of 90° − 47° = 43°. At S2 the line back to S1 has bearing 270°, and the line to L has bearing 352°, so the angle at S2 is 352° − 270° = 82°. The angle at L is 180° − 43° − 82° = 55°. By the law of sines, S2L = 19.833·sin 43°/sin 55° ≈ 16.51 km. The option "14.57" writes 1 hour 25 minutes as 1.25 hours. The option "17.41" takes the angle at S2 as 8°, the angle between the line to L and due north. The option "18.66" uses the bearing 47° itself as the angle at S1.
